In short, this passage teaches us, that though the whole human race was banished from the kingdom of God, the gate of heaven is now opened to us, so that we are fellow-citizens of the saints, and companions of the angels, (Ephesians 2:19;) and that they, having been appointed to be guardians of our salvation, descend from the blessed rest of the heavenly glory
“De la gloire celeste.”
to relieve our distresses.
CHAPTER 2
John 2:1-11
1. Three days after,
“Tertio die;” — “trois jours apres.”
there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there. 2. And Jesus also was invited, and his disciples, to the marriage 3. And when the wine fell short, the mother of Jesus saith to him, They have no wine. 4. Jesus saith to her, What have I to do with thee? my hour is not yet come. 5. His mother saith to the servants, Do whatever he shall bid you. 6. And there were there six water-pots of stone, placed according to the Jewish custom of cleansing, containing each of them about two or three baths. 7. Jesus saith to them, Fill the water-pots with water. And they filled them to the brim. 8. And he saith to them, Draw out now, and carry to the master of the feast; and they carried. 9. And when the master of the feast had tasted the water which was made wine, (and knew not whence it was, but the servants who drew the water knew,) the master of the feast calleth the bridegroom, 10. And saith to him, Every man at first sets down good wine; and when men have drunk freely, then that which is worse; but thou hast kept the good wine till now. 11. This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and displayed his glory, and his disciples believed on him.

For is any thing more ordinary with the <ns0:hi>Chaldee Paraphrast,</ns0:hi> than this Expre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>sion, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 45.12. <ns0:hi>I have made Heaven and Earth,</ns0:hi> Chald. <ns0:hi>I in my word</ns0:hi> have made Heaven and Earth: So chap. 48.13. <ns0:hi>Mine hand hath laid the foun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dation of the earth.</ns0:hi> Chald. <ns0:hi>By my word</ns0:hi> I have laid the foun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dations of the Earth; this is taken from <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi>'s<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> describing the Creation by Gods Word of Command, <ns0:hi>Let there be light, and there was light</ns0:hi>; the manner of expressing it by the Word Command, is significative, that all things were made by his Eternal Word; For would any <ns0:hi>Iew</ns0:hi> deny, that God <ns0:hi>by his Word</ns0:hi> created the World? The Evangelist therefore calleth Christ, to whom <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3. he was about to attribute the Creation, <ns0:hi>the Word</ns0:hi>; not the <ns0:hi>Word of God</ns0:hi> (so the Scriptures are called); to distinguish Christ in this notion <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>om the <ns0:hi>Revelation</ns0:hi> of the Divine Will to the Prophets, he is onely called <ns0:hi>the Word,</ns0:hi> though he was the <ns0:hi>Son of God.</ns0:hi> Nor is it said, That in the beginning was the Word Created (as is said of the <ns0:hi>Heavens</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Ear<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>h,</ns0:hi> Gen. 1.1. but <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> the Word; this proveth the <ns0:hi>eternal existence</ns0:hi> of the second Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son in the Trinity; for what <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> in the beginning, did not then begin to be; the term, <ns0:hi>the Word,</ns0:hi> without the addition of God, speaketh him a <ns0:hi>subsistence</ns0:hi>; and it being said, That in the beginning <ns0:hi>he was,</ns0:hi> speaks his eternal existence; for what had a Being in the Beginning of Time, must needs be <ns0:hi>Eternal,</ns0:hi> nothing being when Time began, but what was Eternal. To this purpose are those Texts, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 90.2. <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 8.22, 23, 24. <ns0:hi>&c. Iohn</ns0:hi> 17.5. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 1.4. 2 <ns0:hi>Thes.</ns0:hi> 2.13. Which two Texts compared, shew <ns0:hi>In the beginning</ns0:hi> here used, to be the same with <ns0:hi>before the foundation of the world</ns0:hi>; so 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.9.</ns0:note>, and the word was with God <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Lest any should say, Where was <ns0:hi>this Word</ns0:hi> before the foundations of the Earth were laid? the Evangelist saith, <ns0:hi>with God</ns0:hi>; which agreeth with <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 8.27, 30. This both distinguisheth Christ from all Creatures, (none of which were <ns0:hi>with God in the beginning</ns0:hi>; and also sheweth the vanity of <ns0:hi>Sabellius,</ns0:hi> and those we call <ns0:hi>Quakers,</ns0:hi> who will not allow Christ to be a distinct subsistence, or Person from his Father; it also denoteth the Sons <ns0:hi>co-exist<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence,</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>equality</ns0:hi> with his Father; and yet, his Filial re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lation; for God is not said to have been with the Word, but the <ns0:hi>Word</ns0:hi> was with <ns0:hi>God,</ns0:hi> which also speaks a perfect unity and consent betwixt them.</ns0:note>, and the word was God <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Lest any should say, What but God can be Eternal? or be said to have been and had an existence in the beginning of the World? the Evan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gelist addeth, That the <ns0:hi>Word</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>God</ns0:hi>; that is, the person or subsistence spoken of, and intended by him, was <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>he Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vine Being, which is but one, tho' in it there be three di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stinct subsistences; all make but <ns0:hi>One</ns0:hi> and the same Divine Being. The first thing spoken here of Christ, attributed to him <ns0:hi>Eternity</ns0:hi>: The second speaks his <ns0:hi>Relation</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi>; this speaks the <ns0:hi>Oneness</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sameness</ns0:hi> of his <ns0:hi>Essence</ns0:hi> with that of the Father. The term <ns0:hi>God,</ns0:hi> which in the foregoing words is to be taken <ns0:hi>personally</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>God the Father,</ns0:hi> is here to be taken <ns0:hi>Essentially,</ns0:hi> as it signifieth the Divine Being.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 The same was <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 1.1.</ns0:note> in the Beginning with God <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">These words of the Evangelist are a farther Confirmati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on and explication of what the Evangelist had said before; asserting the <ns0:hi>Eternity</ns0:hi> of the Son, and his <ns0:hi>Relation to the Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>oneness of Essence</ns0:hi> with the Father; whether the Evangelist forewarned by the Spirit of God, did add this repetition to fore-arm Christians against those Errors which did afterward trouble the Church, I cannot say; but certain it is, That these words do effectually confute the <ns0:hi>Eunomi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ans,</ns0:hi> who distinguished betwixt the Word which in the Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ginning was with God, and that <ns0:hi>Word</ns0:hi> by which all things were made; and the <ns0:hi>Arians,</ns0:hi> who make the Father to have existed before the Son; as also the <ns0:hi>Anomians,</ns0:hi> who would make the Father and the Son diverse both in Nature and Will. Some others make this Verse a transition to the 4th, and the sense to be, This same was not manifest to the World from the Beginning of the World, but was with God until he came to be manifested in the Flesh: Thus 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.2. it is said, <ns0:hi>he was with the father, and was manifested unto us.</ns0:hi> He was <ns0:hi>manifest in the flesh,</ns0:hi> 1 Tim. 3.16.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rev. 4.11.</ns0:note> All things were made by him <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">The Divine Nature, and Eternal existence of the Lord Christ, is evident from his efficiency in the Creation of the World; what the Evangelist here calleth <ns0:hi>All things,</ns0:hi> the Apostle to the <ns0:hi>Hebrews,</ns0:hi> chap. 1.2. calleth <ns0:hi>the Worlds.</ns0:hi> And St. <ns0:hi>Paul, Col.</ns0:hi> 1.16. calleth <ns0:hi>all things that are in heaven and earth, visible and invisible. Moses</ns0:hi> calls the <ns0:hi>heavens and the earth,</ns0:hi> Gen. 1.1. These were <ns0:hi>all</ns0:hi> made by the <ns0:hi>Word</ns0:hi>; no<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> as an Instrumental cause, but as a principal efficient cause; for tho' it be true, that the Preposition <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, is sometimes used to signify an instrumental cause; yet it is as true, that it is often used to signify the principal efficient cause; as <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 6.57. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 5.5. and 11.36. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 4.6. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 3.16. and in ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny other Texts; it here only denoteth the order of the working of the <ns0:hi>Holy Trinity.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>; and with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out him was not any thing made that was made <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Nothing that was made,</ns0:hi> neither the Heavens nor the Earth, neither things visible nor invisible, that were made, were made without him. There is nothing more ordinary in Holy W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>it, than after the lay<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing down an Universal Proposition, (where no <ns0:hi>Synecdoche</ns0:hi> i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> used), to add also an Universal Negative for the confirmati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of it: So <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 3.12. <ns0:hi>There is none good</ns0:hi>; then is added, <ns0:hi>no not one.</ns0:hi> Lam. 2.2. and in many other Texts. The term <ns0:hi>without him,</ns0:hi> doth not exclude the efficiency either of the First or Third Person in the Trinity, in the Creation of all things; the <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi> created the World by the Son, <ns0:hi>His Word</ns0:hi>; and the <ns0:hi>Creation</ns0:hi> of the World is attributed to the <ns0:hi>Spirit, Gen.</ns0:hi> 1.1. <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 33.4. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 33.6.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:328" />4 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.26. 1 Joh. 5.11.</ns0:note> In him was life <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">In this Word was Life <ns0:hi>Corporal, Spiritual, Eternal</ns0:hi>; it was in him as in the Fountain. Some understand this of <ns0:hi>Corporal life,</ns0:hi> both in the first Being and preservation of it; It is certain that this is in Christ, for <ns0:hi>he upholdeth all things by the word of his power,</ns0:hi> Heb. 1.3. Acts 17.28. And thus it is another demonstration of the Deity of Christ. Others think, that here is rather a transition from <ns0:hi>Creation</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />demption</ns0:hi>; you <ns0:hi>hath he quickened,</ns0:hi> Eph. 2.1. Others un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstand it of <ns0:hi>Eternal Life,</ns0:hi> because our Evangelist most ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nerally taketh the term of Life, as a benefit flowing from Christ in this sense, as chap. 3.16. and 4.14. and in a multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tude of other Texts. I know no reason why we should not understand it of all Life; all Life being in Christ, as God equal with the Father; and Spiritual and Eternal Life flow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing also from him in a more peculiar consideration, as Medi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ator.</ns0:note>; and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 8.12. and 9.5. and 12 46.</ns0:note> the life was the light of men <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">But tho' as God he distributes life according to their degree to all his Creatures, yet is he the peculiar <ns0:hi>light of men,</ns0:hi> enlightning their minds with Light, of which Ve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />getative and sensitive Creatures are not capable; so as by <ns0:hi>Light</ns0:hi> is not here to be understood the emanations of any lucid bodies, as that of the Sun or Stars; for other Creatures as well as men are capable of that; nor is it to be under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood of the <ns0:hi>Light of Reason,</ns0:hi> though that be the <ns0:hi>Candle of the Lord</ns0:hi> in the Soul; but that <ns0:hi>Light</ns0:hi> by which we discern the things of God; in which sense the Apostle saith, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 5.8. <ns0:hi>You were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord.</ns0:hi> And therefore he saith of <ns0:hi>men,</ns0:hi> exclusively to <ns0:hi>Angels,</ns0:hi> who, tho lightsom, noble Creatures, yet had not their nature assumed by Christ, Heb. 2.16. Besides that it is said in the next Verse, that this Light <ns0:hi>shined in the darkness,</ns0:hi> that is, amongst ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny men who yet had reasonable Souls, but the <ns0:hi>darkness com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prehended it not.</ns0:hi> That cannot be, that men did not compre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hend Reason, but even rational men comprehended not this Light of supernatural Revelation: So <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> is said to have come to <ns0:hi>Testify of that Light</ns0:hi>; who did not come to testify of Christ, as the <ns0:hi>Author of Reason.</ns0:hi> Nor is there any Text of Scripture in which the term <ns0:hi>Light</ns0:hi> signifieth <ns0:hi>Reason.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.19.</ns0:note> the light <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">He had said before, That Life was in Christ, in him as in the Fountain; and the Life in him was the Light of men, giving Light to men. Now this Light which was in him, had its emanations (as Light in the Sun; and</ns0:note> shineth in darkness <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">the <ns0:hi>darkness,</ns0:hi> that is, men of dark minds, the abstract being put for the con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crete,) comprehended (that is received) it not.</ns0:note>: and the darkness comprehended it not <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">This was true concerning the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> in former times, upon whom Christ the true Light had shined in many Types and Prophecies; it was also true concerning the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> of that present Age, to whom through the favour of him who had undertaken the Redemption of man, the means of Gra<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e were continued; through the blindness of their minds and hardness of their hearts, t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ey wilfully rejected those means of illumination which God granted to them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 ¶ <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matth. 3.1. vers. 33.</ns0:note> There was a man sent from God <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Not the <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> not an <ns0:hi>Angel,</ns0:hi> but a man; yet one, than whom (as our Saviour saith) there had not risen a greater amongst those that were born of Women; he did not come upon his own head, but was sent; for he was he of whom it was written, <ns0:hi>Mal.</ns0:hi> 3.1. <ns0:hi>Behold I will send my messenger before my face,</ns0:hi> &c. Luke 7.27. He was not sent of men, but of God, foretold by the <ns0:hi>Angel,</ns0:hi> as to his existence, name, work, and success, <ns0:hi>L<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ke</ns0:hi> 1.13, 14, 15, 16, 17.</ns0:note>, whose name <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> John <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">His name was <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> named by the Angel, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 1.13. before he was born; by his <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mother, Luk.</ns0:hi> 1.60, 63. when he was born. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> signifieth <ns0:hi>Grace</ns0:hi>; and doubtless the <ns0:hi>Baptist</ns0:hi> obtained that name, because he was to be the first, and a famous Preacher of the Grace of the Gospel which came to the World through Jesus Christ.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 The same came for a witness <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was called a <ns0:hi>Messenger,</ns0:hi> to denote his Authority; a <ns0:hi>Witness,</ns0:hi> to denote his Work which is the work of every true Minister of the Gospel. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was the <ns0:hi>first Witness,</ns0:hi> and Witnessed a thing wholly unknown (before him) to the generality of the World; for though the <ns0:hi>Shepherds,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Simeon</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Anna</ns0:hi> had given some Testimony to Christ, when he was born and brought into the Temple to be offered to the Lord; yet that was Thirty years since, and generally forgot; neither could they bear a Testimony to him as an actual Minister of the Gospel. The <ns0:hi>Apostles</ns0:hi> were to be Wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nesses to Christ, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.8. Witnesses of his <ns0:hi>Resurrection, Acts</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.22. and 4.33. and 5.32. and 10.41. and 13.31. All the <ns0:hi>Prophe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>s,</ns0:hi> Acts 10.43. bare Witness to him, that whosoever believeth in his Name should be saved. So did <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> also; a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>d <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> further pointed to him, passing by, and Witnessed that he was he of whom the Prophets spake. So that the Apostles, and so following Ministers, were, and are greater Witnesses than <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the Baptist. The Prophets witnessed that he should come, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> Baptist witnessed that he was come; the Apostles witnessed that he was not only come, but had Died, and was again risen from the Dead.</ns0:note>, to bear wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness of the light <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">For <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Office was to give a Testimony to Christ the true Light, mentioned before; so called, because he <ns0:hi>maketh ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifest,</ns0:hi> Eph. 5.13. He <ns0:hi>revealeth</ns0:hi> his Father, Matth. 11.27. He is <ns0:hi>the brightness of his fathers glory,</ns0:hi> Heb. 1.3. who is <ns0:hi>Light,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.5. and the World is by him inlightned. It was Prophesied, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 11.9. of his times, That <ns0:hi>the Earth should be full of the knowledg of the Lord.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">The end of <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Testimony was, That multitudes of all sorts might believe by him, or by it, as an instrumental cause of their Faith. If we read it <ns0:hi>by him,</ns0:hi> it is most proper to understand the Pronoun of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptist</ns0:hi>; for we are not said to be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieve <ns0:hi>by Christ,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>in him, in his name,</ns0:hi> &c.</ns0:note>, that all men through him might believe <ns0:hi>r.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 He was not that light <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptist</ns0:hi> was a Light, as all Saints are <ns0:hi>light in the Lord,</ns0:hi> Eph. 5.8. Nay, in a peculiar sense our Saviour beareth him Witness, that <ns0:hi>he was a burning and shining light</ns0:hi>; but he was not <ns0:hi>that light</ns0:hi> before mentioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 5. <ns0:hi>that shineth in darkness</ns0:hi>; and again <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 9. which lighteth <ns0:hi>every one that cometh into the World. Iohn</ns0:hi> borrowed his Light from that <ns0:hi>Original Light</ns0:hi>; that Light was God, he was but <ns0:hi>a man</ns0:hi> sent <ns0:hi>from God.</ns0:hi> The men of the World are ordinarily in extreams, either wholly rejecting Gods Ministers and Wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nesses, or else adoring them; as the World is concerned to take heed of the former, so the Ministers of Christ are also highly concerned not to admit the latter. See <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 7.33. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 14.13, 14. but both <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> here, and <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> there, were very cautious not to rob their Master of the honour due unto him alone.</ns0:note>, but <ns0:hi>was sent</ns0:hi> to bear witness of that light <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> as was said before, came onely to bear Witness of <ns0:hi>that Light,</ns0:hi> that he was come, and shi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned forth, and was the true Light, as it followeth.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Vers. 4.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>That</ns0:hi> was the true Light <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">True is sometimes opposed to what is false, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 4.25. sometimes to what is <ns0:hi>Typical</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Figurative, Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.17. Sometimes to what is not <ns0:hi>Original,</ns0:hi> and of it self; in Oppo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sition to all these Christ is the <ns0:hi>True Light</ns0:hi>; he who alone deserved the name of <ns0:hi>Light,</ns0:hi> having Light in himself, and from himself, 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 2.8. and shining more gloriously than the Prophets or Apostles.</ns0:note>, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">He lighteth not the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> only (as the Prophets of old) but both the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentiles.</ns0:hi> Some understand this of the <ns0:hi>Light of Reason</ns0:hi>; but besides, that <ns0:hi>Reason</ns0:hi> is no where in Holy Writ called <ns0:hi>Light</ns0:hi>; nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther did this illumination agree to Christ as Mediator. It is rather therefore to be understood of the <ns0:hi>Light of Gospel Revelation,</ns0:hi> which Christ caused to be made to all the World, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 28.19. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 16.15. Those who Interpret it of the more internal illumination <ns0:hi>by</ns0:hi> the Holy Spirit of God, by which Christ is not revealed <ns0:hi>to us</ns0:hi> onely, but <ns0:hi>in us,</ns0:hi> say, That Christ hath done what lay in him (as a Mini<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ster of the Gospel) so to inlighten all that came into the World; and that Christ is said to inlighten every man, because none is inlightened but by him; and that some of all sorts are by him inlightned; in one of which two lat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter Senses, the terms <ns0:hi>All</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Every man</ns0:hi> must be Interpret<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed in a multitude of Texts in the Gospel. The words in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> are so, as they may either be Translated as we read them, or thus, <ns0:hi>Who coming into the world, enlight<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned every man.</ns0:hi> A more universal Spiritual Light, or means to come to the Knowledg of God, overspreading the World after Christs coming, than before. So <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 12.46. <ns0:hi>I am come a Light into the World.</ns0:hi> And it is by some observed, that the Phrase, <ns0:hi>coming into the world,</ns0:hi> doth not barely signify a being born, but being <ns0:hi>sent into the world by the father,</ns0:hi> being <ns0:hi>sanctified,</ns0:hi> as in <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 10.36. and 17, 18.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 He was in the world <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">He was in the place called the <ns0:hi>World,</ns0:hi> and amongst the men of the World; for so the term <ns0:hi>World</ns0:hi> is often <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 16.28. 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 3.6. Christ before he came in the Flesh, was in it; filling both the Heavens and the Earth, and sustaining it by the Word of his Power, and mani<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />festing his Will to it, more immediately to <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> and to the <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi>; and more <ns0:hi>mediately</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> and by the <ns0:hi>Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Heb. 1.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. and 11.3.</ns0:note> the world was made by him <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">And the Heavens and the Earth, all things visible and invisible (as was said before) were made by him. And</ns0:note>; and the world knew him not <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">the men of the World took no notice of him, did not acknowledg him, believe in him, nor were subject to him; so the word <ns0:hi>know</ns0:hi> often signifies (according to the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> idiom) <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 10.14, 15, 27. Not a bare comprehension of an Object in the Understanding, but sui<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>able affections: So <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 7.23. 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 3.1. This is not to be understood of all individual persons in the World; for <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and many particular persons, did in this sense know him; but the generality of the World did not. The Heathens did not (who are sometimes called <ns0:hi>the World,</ns0:hi> distinctively from the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 2.2. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 1.21.) and most of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> did not, tho' some did.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:328" />11 He came unto his own <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Christ came into the World, which being made by him, was in the most proper sense his own; or, to the <ns0:hi>Israelites,</ns0:hi> which were as his own House, Land and Possession, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 85.1. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 16.32. The <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> word is in the <ns0:hi>Plural Number,</ns0:hi> and used in the places before mentioned, as also <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 21.6. Sometimes signifying mens proper Country, sometimes their proper house. But it is a farther question, what coming is here spoken of; tho' it be generally (or by many at least) interpreted of Christs coming by his Incarnation, yet that seemeth not to be the sense; partly, because that co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ming is spoken of, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. And partly, because in that sense the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> did receive him; nor was it in their power to hin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der his manifestation in the flesh. The <ns0:hi>coming</ns0:hi> therefore here mentioned, seemeth to be intended of his coming by his <ns0:hi>Prophets, Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptist,</ns0:hi> and his own personal Preaching of the Gospel.</ns0:note>, and his own re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceived him not <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Whom in this way of coming, they did not receive, believing neither the Testimony given by his Prophets, nor by the <ns0:hi>Baptist,</ns0:hi> nor by himself, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 5.43.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 56.5. Rom. 8.15. 2 Pet. 1.4. 1 John 3.1.</ns0:note> as many as received him <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Though the generality of those amongst whom Christ came, received him not in the manner before expressed; yet some did own him, believed in him, and submitted to him; and to as many as thus <ns0:hi>received</ns0:hi> him, not into their Houses onely, but into their Hearts.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">He gave a Pow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er, or a Right, or Priviledg; not that they might if they would be; but <ns0:hi>to be</ns0:hi> actually, to become, or be the Sons of God by <ns0:hi>Adoption</ns0:hi>; for Believers are already the <ns0:hi>Sons of God,</ns0:hi> Gal. 3.26. Though it doth not yet appear what they shall be in the <ns0:hi>Adoption,</ns0:hi> mentioned <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.23. which the Apostle calls the <ns0:hi>Redemption of the body, viz.</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Resurrection</ns0:hi>; hence <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 20.36. the Children of God are called the <ns0:hi>Children of the Resurrection.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, to them gave he <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>right, or priviledg.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> power to become the sons of God <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">This is the Priviledg of all that <ns0:hi>believe</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>name of Christ</ns0:hi>; by which term he opens the former term of <ns0:hi>Receiving:</ns0:hi> To receive Christ, and to believe in his Name, are the same thing. To believe in his <ns0:hi>Name,</ns0:hi> is either to <ns0:hi>believe in him, Acts</ns0:hi> 3.26. or in the <ns0:hi>Revelation</ns0:hi> of himself in the <ns0:hi>Promi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses of the Gospel.</ns0:hi> The proposition of Gods Word is the object of <ns0:hi>Faith of assent</ns0:hi>; but the person of the <ns0:hi>Mediator</ns0:hi> is the object of that Faith which receiveth Christ; and those alone have a Right to be the Sons of God, and to the Priviledges peculiar to Sons, who believe in Christ as revealed in the Promises of the word of God, and there exhibited to men.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> to them that believe on his name <ns0:hi>e.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.5. James 1.8.</ns0:note>13 Which were born, not of blood <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>Bloods.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Not of the Blood of Men and Women; or not of the Blood of <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> (which was the boast of the <ns0:hi>Iews, we have Abraham to our Father</ns0:hi>).</ns0:note>, nor of the will of the flesh <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Nor from the Lusts of the Flesh.</ns0:note>, nor of the will of man <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Nor from a power in mans Will, or mens free act in adopting other mens Children. To be <ns0:hi>born,</ns0:hi> sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifieth <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>o receive our principle of Life; those who are the Children of God have not the Principle of their Life, as they are such, from the motions of nature, nor from the Will of men.</ns0:note>, but of God <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>But of God,</ns0:hi> whatever be the sense of the former Words, these Words plainly affirm God to be the <ns0:hi>principal efficient,</ns0:hi> and procreant cause of all those who are the Sons of God; for Faith, by which <ns0:hi>we are the children of God,</ns0:hi> Gal. 3.26. is the work of God, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 6.29. His Gift, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 1.29. and men are <ns0:hi>born again, not of corruptible seed, but that which is incorruptible,</ns0:hi> 1 Pet. 1.23. <ns0:hi>They are san<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctified and cleansed with the washing of water by the word,</ns0:hi> Eph. 5.26. <ns0:hi>The washing of regeneration, and renewing of the holy ghost,</ns0:hi> Titus 3.5.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matth. 1.16. Luke 1.31. and 2.7.</ns0:note> And the word was made flesh <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">The Son of God, called <ns0:hi>the Word,</ns0:hi> for the reasons be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore specified, was made truly man, as flesh often signifieth in Holy Writ, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 6.12. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 65.2. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 40.5, 6. Not a vile, despicable, mortal man. The Evangelist rather saith he was made Flesh, than he was made man; more plainly to distinguish the two Natures in Christ, to assert the truth of his Humane Nature; to let us know that Christ assumed Hu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mane Nature in common, not the particular nature of any; to commend the Love of God, and to let us see, That his Plaister was proportioned to our Sore, it reached all Flesh. The Evangelist saith not, he was changed into Flesh; but, by assuming he was made Flesh.</ns0:note>, and dwelt amongst us <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">And he Tabe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>nacled amongst us; amongst us men, or amongst men that were his Disciples: The word signifieth properly, he made no long stay.</ns0:note>, (and <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">Math. 17.2. 2 Pet. 1.17.</ns0:note> we beheld his glory <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">And we beheld the signs and effects of his Glory; many of which were seen, both at the time of his Transfiguration, and at his Passion, Resurrection and Ascen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion; the Glory of his Grace, Ho<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>iness, Truth, Miraculous Operations, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, the glory as of the onely begotten of the father) <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Which Glory was the Glory of the onely begotten of the Father; for the particle [<ns0:hi>as</ns0:hi>] here doth not signify Likeness, but Truth; <ns0:hi>Nehemiah</ns0:hi> 7.2. <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 24.14.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Col. 1.19. & 23, 9.</ns0:note> full of grace and truth <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Full of Grace and Truth, as he was God manifested in the flesh. <ns0:hi>Grace</ns0:hi> signifieth Love and Good Will, out of which it was that he delivered us from the Curse and Rigour of the Law (to which Grace is opposed). He was also full of <ns0:hi>Truth,</ns0:hi> both as Truth is opposed to Falshood, and is opposed to the Shadows and Figures of the Law; and Christ was full of Truth, as he was the Anti-type to all the Ceremonies, and all the Promi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses had and have their complement and reality in him. See chap. 14.17. 2 Cor. 1.20. Rom. 15.8. Truth also may signify the <ns0:hi>sincerity</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>integrity</ns0:hi> of Christs Life, as he was without guile.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 ¶ John bare witness of him, and cryed, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was not he, but only a Witness to him, and he continueth to bear Witness, (the Verb is in the present Tense) nor did he give an obscure or cold Testimony, but an open, and plain, and fervent Testimony, according to the Prophecies, his <ns0:hi>Testimony</ns0:hi> was the Voice of one crying in the Wilderness.</ns0:note>
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">ver. 27, 30. & chap. 3.31.</ns0:note>: This was he of whom I spake <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">He first testified that Christ was he of whom he had before spoken; possibly when he was Preaching in the Wilderness, and Christ came to him to be Baptized of him, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 3.11, 14.</ns0:note>, He that co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />meth after me is pre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>erred before me <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">He that cometh after me, in order of time, or in the Ministerial Office and Em<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ployment, or, as if he were my Disciple, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 8.12. is be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />come, or is made before me.</ns0:note>: for he was before me <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">For he was before me, both in the Eternal destination, and in respect of his Divine Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture; as also in <ns0:hi>Dignity</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Eminency,</ns0:hi> considered as a Prophet; <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> one that Revealeth my Fathers Will. This <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> said before, though not in terms, yet in effect; when he said, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 3.11. <ns0:hi>He that cometh after me, is mightier than I, whose shooes I am not worthy to bear,</ns0:hi> &c. So <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 1.7. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 3.16. This is the first thing which is here mention<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, as <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>'s Testimony concerning Christ, respecting the excellency of his person.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 And of his <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Col. 1.19. & 2.9, 10.</ns0:note> fulness have all we received <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Of that plenty of Grace which Christ hath, (who hath not <ns0:hi>the Spirit given him by measure,</ns0:hi> chap. 3.34. as other Saints have, Acts 2.4, 6, 8.) <ns0:hi>We</ns0:hi> who by Nature are void of <ns0:hi>Grace,</ns0:hi> whether taken for the favour of God, or gracious habits, have <ns0:hi>received</ns0:hi> as the Skirts of <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s Garment re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceived the Oil which was plentifully poured out on <ns0:hi>Aarons</ns0:hi> head.</ns0:note>, and grace for grace <ns0:note n="‡" place="bottom">Nor have we received Drops, but <ns0:hi>Grace upon Grace</ns0:hi>; not onely Knowledg and Instruction, but the Love and Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vour of God, and Spiritual habits, in proportion to the fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vour and grace which Christ hath (allowing for our shor<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> capacities); we have received <ns0:hi>Grace freely</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>plentifully,</ns0:hi> all from Christ, and for his sake; which lets us see how much the Grace-receiving Soul is bound to acknowledg and adore Christ, and may be confirmed in the receiving of further Grace, and the hopes of Eternal Life; and it may mind all (according to that of the Apostle, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 6.1.) to take heed that they <ns0:hi>receive not the grace of God in vain.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 For the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ex. 20.1. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Law was given by Moses <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The Law Moral and Ceremonial came not by <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> but was given by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> as Gods Minister and Servant, that Law by which no man can he justified, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 3.28. In this was <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> his honour, of whom you glory, chap. 5.46. God indeed made an eminent use of him, as his Minister; by whom he revealed his Will to you; both in matters of his Worship, according to that Dispensation; and in mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters which concern you in your whole Conversation; but yet there is an eminent difference betwixt him and Jesus Christ. The law is no where called <ns0:hi>Grace,</ns0:hi> neither doth it discover any thing but Duty and Wrath; it sheweth no <ns0:hi>re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mission,</ns0:hi> in case that Duty be not done; nor affordeth strength for the doing of it.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>b<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t</ns0:hi> grace and truth came by Jesus Christ <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">All <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> is from Christ, all the favour of God for the Remission and Pardon of Sin, and for strength and assistance to the performance of Duty, is (not given from God by Christ, as the Law by <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> but) from Christ, as the Fountain of Grace; And not <ns0:hi>Grace</ns0:hi> onely, but <ns0:hi>Truth,</ns0:hi> whether taken for solid and real mercy, or with respect to the Law; the fulfilling of all the <ns0:hi>Types</ns0:hi> and Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phecies in it, was by and in Christ.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 10.2. 1 Tim. 6.16.1 1 John 4.12.</ns0:note> No man hath seen God at any time <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">No man hath at any time seen the Essence of God with his Eyes, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 4.24. Nor with the eyes of his mind under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood the whole Counsel and Will of God, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 11.7. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 11.34. <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> indeed saw the Image and represen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tation of God, and had a more familiar converse with God than others; upon which account he is said to have talked with God <ns0:hi>face to face,</ns0:hi> Numb. 12.7, 8. God sa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>th <ns0:hi>he would speak unto him mouth to mouth, even apparently</ns0:hi>; but he tells us how in the same Verse, <ns0:hi>and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold</ns0:hi>; and God who had spoke to the same sense, Exod. 33.11. saith, v. 20. <ns0:hi>Thou canst not see my face, for there shall no man see me and live.</ns0:hi> Now to whom he did not discover his face, he certainly did not discover all his secret Counsels.</ns0:note>: the onely begotten son, which is in the bosome of the Father <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">But he who is the onely begotten and beloved Son, hath such an intimate Communion with him in his Nature, and such a free Communication of all his Counsels, as it may be said, he is continually in his Bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />som.</ns0:note>, he hath declared <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="†" place="bottom">Hath declared him, not onely as a Prophet decla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />reth the Mind and Will of God, but as <ns0:hi>the Heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament sheweth his handy works,</ns0:hi> Psal. 19.1. Being <ns0:hi>the brightness of his fathers glory, and the express Image of his person,</ns0:hi> Heb. 1.3. So as the Father can onely be seen in the Son; nor is so full a Revela<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of the Fathers Will to be expected from any, as from the Son.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:329" />19 And this is <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.33.</ns0:note> the record of John, when the Jews sent Priests and Levites from Jerusalem, to ask him, Who art thou <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>'s former Testimony was more private to the com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon people; this Testimony was given to a publick Au<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thority. The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> (most probably the Rulers of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> who made up their <ns0:hi>Sanhedrim,</ns0:hi> or great Court, answering a <ns0:hi>Parliament</ns0:hi> with us, for the cognisance of <ns0:hi>false Prophets</ns0:hi> belonged to them) sent <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Levites,</ns0:hi> which <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 24. were <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> of the strictest Sect of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> as to Rites and Ceremonies; these came from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> where the <ns0:hi>Sanhedrim</ns0:hi> constantly sate; and the Chief Priests were (if the Message were not from the <ns0:hi>Sanhedrim</ns0:hi> it self) to ask <ns0:hi>Iohn Baptist</ns0:hi> who he was; that is, by what Authority he Preached and Baptized? What kind of Prophet he was? for they could not but know his Name and Family, he de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scending from a Priest amongst them; and this appeareth to be their sense from what followeth.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 And he <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.28. Acts 13.25.</ns0:note> confessed <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">He being asked openly and plainly, professed, and</ns0:note>, and denied not <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">did not dissemble nor halt in his Speech. These Negatives are in Scripture often added to affirmatives, to exclude all Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceptions. <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 5.17. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 40.10, 11, 12.</ns0:note>; but confessed <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">He did not tell them once so, but again and again, because many were mu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing about it, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 3 15.</ns0:note>, I am not the Christ <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">I am not that great <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> which God hath promised you, and in the expectation of whom you live, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 2.26, 38. & 19.11. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 4.25. The <ns0:hi>Diligence</ns0:hi> we shall constantly observe in the Servants of God in Holy Writ, to avoid the arrogating of that Honour to themselves, which is due onely to God and Christ; and this, together with <ns0:hi>Iohn's</ns0:hi> steadiness and plainness, doth very well become all Professors, but the Ministers of the Gospel espe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLunhyphen" />cially.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And they asked him, What then? Art thou Elias <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was at <ns0:hi>Bethabara</ns0:hi> when these Messengers came to him, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 28. they asked him if he were <ns0:hi>Elias.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had not onely an expectation of the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> but of <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi> to come as a Messenger before him, according to the Prophecy, <ns0:hi>Mal.</ns0:hi> 4.5. as appeareth, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 17.10. <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 9.11. of which they had a gross Conception here, That <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi> should come, out of Heaven personally, or at least that his <ns0:hi>Soul</ns0:hi> should come into another Body (according to the <ns0:hi>Pithagorian</ns0:hi> Opi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nion) now the meaning of the Prophecy was, That one should come like <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> and this was fulfilled in <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> Luke 1.17. as our Saviour tells us, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 17.12. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 9.13. but they asked the Question according to that notion they had of <ns0:hi>Elias.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>? And he saith, I am not <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">To which <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> answereth, that he was not neither that <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi> that ascended in a Fiery Chariot to Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven; nor any body informed with <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi>'s Soul, (and thus the words of our Saviour, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 17.12. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 9.12. are easily reconciled to this Text.)</ns0:note>. Art thou <ns0:note place="margin">A Prophet.</ns0:note> that Prophet <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">They go on, and ask him if he were <ns0:hi>that Prophet,</ns0:hi> or a Prophet? Some think that he meant the Prophet promised, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 18.18. but that was no other than Christ himself, which he had before denied him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self to be; nor doth it appear from any Text of Scripture, that the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had any expectation of any other parti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cular Prophet; but it is plain from <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 9.8. that they had a notion that it was possible one of the old Prophets might rise again from the Dead, for so they guessed there con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning Christ: But others think that the article in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> here is not emphatical; and they onely asked him if he were a <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi>; for the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had a general notion, that the Spirit of Prophecy had left them ever since the times of <ns0:hi>Zechariah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Malachy</ns0:hi>; which they hoped was return<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed in <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptist,</ns0:hi> and about this they question him, if he were a Prophet?</ns0:note>? And he answered, No <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">To which he answereth, <ns0:hi>No,</ns0:hi> Neither that <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> promised, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 18.18. nor yet any of the old Prophets risen from the dead; nor yet one like the Prophets of the Old Testament, who onely Prophecied of a Christ to come; but as Christ calls him, Matth. 11.9. <ns0:hi>More than a Prophet,</ns0:hi> one who shewed and declared to them a Christ already come; for the Law and the Prophets Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phecied but until <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>; the Law in its Types foreshewing, the <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> in their Sermons foretelling a <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> to come, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> did more. His Father indeed, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 1.76. called him <ns0:hi>the Prophet of the highest</ns0:hi>; but there <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> is to be un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood not in a strict, but in a large sense, as the term Prophecy is taken, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 12.6. And the term <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> often signifieth one that revealeth the Will of God to men; in which large sense <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was a <ns0:hi>Prophet,</ns0:hi> and yet more than a <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> in the stricter notion of the term; and in that sense No Prophet, that is, no meer Prophet; so <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 11.19. <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> tells the people <ns0:hi>they s<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ould not eat flesh one, or two, or five, or ten, or twenty days,</ns0:hi> because they should eat it a whole Month together.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 Then said they unto him, Who art thou <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Hitherto <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> had given them onely a <ns0:hi>Negative answer,</ns0:hi> and told them who he was not; he was neither Christ, nor the <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> nor that Prophet they expected; neither any of the old Prophets risen from the Dead; nor any Prophet at all in a strict sense (as were the Prophets of the Old Testa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment); they press him to a direct, plain, positive Answer.</ns0:note>? that we may give an answer to them that sent us <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">That they might give an Answer to those that sent them, who did not send them to enquire what he was not, but what he was.</ns0:note>. What saist thou of thy self <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">And there were various talks and discourses of the People about him, which they were not willing to take up and run away with; but they desired to have it from himself.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luc. 3.4. Isa. 40.3.</ns0:note> He said, I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Esaias <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">We had the same, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 3.3. <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 1.3. See the Notes there. <ns0:hi>Chemnitius</ns0:hi> thinks, that <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> chose rather to preach, and fulfil his Ministry in the Wilderness, than in the Temple; to make an illustrious difference betwixt himself, who was but the Lords Messenger, and whose Office was but to pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pare the Lords way, and his Lord himself, of whom it was Prophecied, <ns0:hi>Mal.</ns0:hi> 3.1. <ns0:hi>The Lord, whom you seek, shall sud<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />denly come to his Holy Temple</ns0:hi>; upon which account <ns0:hi>Haggai</ns0:hi> prophecied, <ns0:hi>Haggai</ns0:hi> 2.9. <ns0:hi>That the Glory</ns0:hi> of that latter house (builded by <ns0:hi>Ezra,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Zerobabel,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Nehemiah) should be greater than of the former.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 And they which were sent, were of the Pharisees <ns0:note n="(p)" place="bottom">Who these Pharisees were, hath been before explain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed in our Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 3.7. They were of the strictest Sect of the Jewish Religion, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 26.5. The greatest part of their Counce<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s was made up of those of this Sect, as may be learned from <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 23. They were the men most Zealous for, and tenacious of the <ns0:hi>Iewish Rites</ns0:hi>; and would allow nothing to be added to the Jewish Worship to what they had received concerning it, either from the Law of God, or the Traditions o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> the Elders.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 And they asked him, and said unto him, Why Baptizest thou then, if thou be not that Christ, nor Elias, neither that Prophet <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">The Pharisees themselves would allow the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>Prophet,</ns0:hi> to make any additions to, or alterati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons in the Worship of God, but none else: Hence it is, they ask, by what Authority he Baptized, if he were none of these? From whence we may learn, That although they might have some umbrage of that Baptismal washing which was under the Gospel, to commence into a Sacrament, or foederal sign in the washing of their Proselites, or of Jewish Children when they were Circumcised; yet <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>'s Action was looked upon as new, who Baptized adult Jews; now the care of the <ns0:hi>Sanhedrim</ns0:hi> was to keep the Worship of God incorrupt, and the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> amongst them had a par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ticular Zeal in the case, especially so far as the <ns0:hi>Traditions</ns0:hi> of the Elders were concerned.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 John answered them, saying <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">This was no strict Answer to their Question; which was not, how, but why he Baptized? But proper Replies, are often called Answers in Scripture, though not apposite to the Question.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note place="margin">Matth. 3.11.</ns0:note> I baptize with water: <ns0:note n="†" place="bottom">I Baptize you with meer Water</ns0:note> but there standeth one amongst you, whom you know not <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">but there hath stood one amongst you, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, or (by an usual putting<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>of one Tense for another) there standeth one; Christ had been there with the Crowd, <ns0:hi>Luc.</ns0:hi> 3.15, 21. and pos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sibly was amongst them still, when <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> spake these words, whom you know not (not so much as <ns0:hi>ore tenus</ns0:hi> by Face.)</ns0:note>;</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27. He <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 3.11. ver. 15, 30. Mar. 1.8. Luke 3.26. ch. 1.15. Act. 19.4.</ns0:note> it is, who coming after me is preferred before me <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist,</ns0:hi> had before told them, <ns0:hi>He that com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth after me, is preferred before me.</ns0:hi> See the Notes there. He now repeateth those words; and it is observable, that the three other Evangelists all put this Passage before the Histo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry of Christ's coming to him to be Baptized. So as it is probable, that these Messengers came to <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> as he was Baptizing, and either immediately before or after Christ's Baptism, Christ being yet in the Croud, he repeateth to his hearers, what he had a little before said of him, that he was to be preferred before him.</ns0:note>, whose shoo's latchet I am not wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thy to unloose <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">He here inlargeth upon it with a <ns0:hi>Proverbial Speech,</ns0:hi> which the other Evangelists have, with a very little variation; <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>whose Shoo's I am not worthy to bear:</ns0:hi> that is, to perform unto him the very meanest Service or Office. We have such forms of Speeches in use at this day amongst us, when we would ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />press the great pre-eminence of some one above another; we say of that other, <ns0:hi>He is not worthy to tye his Shoo's</ns0:hi>; Or, <ns0:hi>to carry his Shoo's after him.</ns0:hi> There is a vast difference be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tween Christ, and the most excellent of his Ministers; which as to Baptism lieth here; the Ministerial Baptism is but with Water; Christ Baptizeth with the <ns0:hi>Holy Ghost,</ns0:hi> and fire, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 3.11. or with the Holy Ghost, as <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 1.8.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:329" />28 These things were done in Bethabara beyond Jordan <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The Evangelist had before told us what was done, these words tell us where. Some ancient Writers will have the place to have been <ns0:hi>Bethany</ns0:hi>; but they seem not to have so well considered <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 11.18. where <ns0:hi>Bethany</ns0:hi> is said to have been but <ns0:hi>fifteen Furlongs from Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and conse<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quently on this side <ns0:hi>Iordan</ns0:hi>; whereas the <ns0:hi>Evangelist</ns0:hi> saith, that this place was <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>beyond Iordan,</ns0:hi> in the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Reuben,</ns0:hi> in the Country of <ns0:hi>Peraea,</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, where John was Baptizing <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">where <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> at this time was <ns0:hi>Baptizing,</ns0:hi> and probably had been so for some time.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 ¶ The next day <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The most think, the day following that day, when the Messengers from <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> had been examining the <ns0:hi>Baptist. Heinsius</ns0:hi> thinks it was the same day, and saith, the <ns0:hi>Hellenists</ns0:hi> usually so interprets <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> for <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, after these things; but the former Sense is more generally embraced.</ns0:note>, John seeth Jesus coming to him <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> seeth Jesus coming to him out of the Wilderness, (as some think) where he had been tempted by the Devil; but then it must follow, that he was not amongst the Croud, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 26. standing in the midst of them when the Messengers were there; and it should appear by <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 32, and 33. that this which is here recorded happened after Christs <ns0:hi>Baptism</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> (of which this <ns0:hi>Evangelist</ns0:hi> saith nothing); it seemeth rather to be understood of another coming of Christ to <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> after he had been Baptized.</ns0:note>, and saith, Behold <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 53.7. Act. 8.32.</ns0:note> the <ns0:note n="‡" place="bottom">When <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> seeing<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> him, pointed as it were with his Finger to him (for the term <ns0:hi>Behold</ns0:hi> seemeth to be here used demonstra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tively) shewing them the person whom he would have them cast their Eye upon; whom he calls,</ns0:note> lamb of God <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">the lamb of God, not onely to denote his excellency, as we read of the <ns0:hi>Night of the Lord, Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.42. and the <ns0:hi>bread of God, Lev.</ns0:hi> 21.21. which indeed Christ was, being <ns0:hi>without Ble<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mish.</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.19. But with reference to the Lambs used in the Jewish Sacrifices, not only at the Passover, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.5. but in the daily Sacrifice, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 29.38. <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 1.10. or the <ns0:hi>Burnt Offering,</ns0:hi> and in the <ns0:hi>Peace Offering, Levit.</ns0:hi> 3.7. and in the <ns0:hi>Sin Offering, Levit.</ns0:hi> 4.32. he calls Christ, the <ns0:hi>Lamb</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>God,</ns0:hi> probably, because divers of the Priests were there to hear; and (as appears, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 39.) it was nigh the time of their daily Sacrifice, that so he might mind them, that Christ was the Truth and Anti-Type to all their Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifices,</ns0:note>, which <ns0:note place="margin">or beareth.</ns0:note> taketh away the sin of the world <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, The word signifies, both to <ns0:hi>take up,</ns0:hi> and to take away; that taketh away the Sins of the World, as God (to whom it belongs to forgive Sin) and this he did by taking them upon himself (so it is Translated, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 16.24.) expiating them, which expiation is followed by a Plenary remission, and taking them away, both the punishment of them, and the root, and body, and power of them; Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deeming them as from the Grave and Hell due to Man for Sin; so from a <ns0:hi>Vain Conversation,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.18. and not doing this for the Jews only, but for the Gentiles also, 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 2.2. for many in the World, being he, without whom there is no remission, <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 4.12. Nor doth his gracious act cease at any time, it is a work he is always doing, and which none but he can do: Ministers may perswade, Priests of old offered Lambs and other Beasts in Sacrifice; but he alone taketh away Sin. So that, as what he said to the Messengers of the <ns0:hi>Sanhedrim,</ns0:hi> gave all the honour of any valuable effect of Baptism to Christ: So, what he saith here, gives him all the honour of any good effect of Preaching, or any good effect of our Ministry; it is he alone, who (when we have said or done what we can) taketh away the sin of the World.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 This is he, of whom I said <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">And (saith he) this is he of whom<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> I said, (as <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 15.) he <ns0:hi>cometh after me</ns0:hi> in order of Time and Ministry, but is more excellent than Iam. See the Notes on <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 15.</ns0:note>, After me com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />etha man, which is preferred before me: for he was before me.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 And I knew him not <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">This verse is best expounded by <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 33. where the same words are repeated, <ns0:hi>I knew him not</ns0:hi>; and is added, <ns0:hi>but he that sent me to baptize with water, the same said unto me, Vpon whom thou shalt see the spirit descend<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing,</ns0:hi> &c. Lest any should think that Christ and <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> had compacted together to give one another credit, or that there was some near relation betwixt <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> and Christ, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> saith, I knew him not, for Christ had spent his time at home, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 2.51. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> had lived in desert places, the Providence of God so ordering it, that <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> should not know Christ, so much as by face, until that time came, when Christ was to be made manifest to <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>: but that he should be made manifest unto Israel <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">But that God might make his Son manifest unto <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> when God by an extraordinary mission sent <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> to Baptize with Water, he gave him this token, That he upon whom he should see the Spirit descending and remaining on him, as <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 33. that was the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> the Lamb of God, that should take away the Sin of the World; he <ns0:hi>who should baptize with the holy ghost.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, therefore am I come baptizing with water <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">And therefore (saith <ns0:hi>Iohn) I came baptizing with water.</ns0:hi> I did not run without sending, nor introduce a new rite or Sacrament without Commission; but being thus sent of God, and that I might give Christ an opportunity of coming to me, that I might see the Spirit descending and remaining upon him. From whence we learn, That none but Christ can in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stitute a Sacrament. <ns0:hi>Iohn Baptized</ns0:hi> not, till he was sent to <ns0:hi>Baptize with Water.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matt. 3.16.</ns0:note> And John bare record saying, I saw the spirit descending from heaven <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Saith <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> According to the Revelation which I had, when I received my extraordinary Commission to Baptize, so it fell out to me, <ns0:hi>I did see,</ns0:hi> when he was baptized, the <ns0:hi>Heaven opening,</ns0:hi> and a representation of the Spirit of God, (for no man can see God and live) descending.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 1.10. Luk. 3.22.</ns0:note>, like a dove <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The form of the Representation, was like that of a Dove.</ns0:note>, and it abode upon him <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">And it was not a meer transient sight, but it did for some time abide upon that Person, in that sensible Representa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion; by that Token I knew that he was the Son of God.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 And I knew him not <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">I was a stranger to him, I knew him in a Sense, when I <ns0:hi>leapt in my Mothers Womb,</ns0:hi> upon his Mothers coming to see my Mother, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 1.41. but that (as Impressions made upon Infants use to do), wore off.</ns0:note>: but he that sent me to baptize with water <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">I had some Im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pression upon me at that time, when he came towards me to be Baptized, which made me say to him, as <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 3.14<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me</ns0:hi>? But yet I was not certain, tho I knew he was in the croud of people, that he was the Person designed, and whose work it should be to Baptize with the Holy Ghost.</ns0:note>, the same said unto me, Upon whom thou shalt see the spirit descending, and remaining on him, the same is he which bap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tizeth with the holy Ghost <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Until the same God, that had given me that Sign, fulfilled it to me.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 And I saw <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">But when I saw that, I could not butbelieve.</ns0:note>, and bare record <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">And also bear an open Testimony to the World, That this man was not meer man, but the eternal Son of that God, who sent me to Baptize with Water; reserving still to himself the Divine Power of blessing that Holy Sacrament, and conferring the Holy Ghost in rege<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nerating habits, working like <ns0:hi>fire,</ns0:hi> in purging away the dross of Souls, and like Water washing away the filth of Sin, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 3.11. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3.5.</ns0:note>, that this is the Son of God.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 ¶ Again the next day after <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">The next day after that the Messengers who came from <ns0:hi>Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> had been with <ns0:hi>Iohn.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, John stood, and two of his disciples.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 And looking upon<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Jesus as he walked <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> stood with two of his Disciples, whether he was Preaching or no, it is not said; but <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> standing with them, saw Christ walking, whence, or whither, is not said; but as a good man is always taking opportunity to commend Christ to others; so <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, he said <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 29.</ns0:note>, Behold the lamb of God <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">upon this occasion, took advan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tage further to make Christ known to those two men (who they were, we shall hear in the following Verses), and re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />peats the words he had said before <ns0:hi>Behold the Lamb of God.</ns0:hi> (See the Notes on <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 27.) Thus good and faithful Ministers will continually be inviting their Disciples to Christ, taking them off from further consideration of themselves, and as Ministers to shew them the way to Christ.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 And the two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">God blessed the verbal Testimony that <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> had gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, so far, that they stood in no need of any Miracle to comfirm it, but upon their hearing <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> speak, they fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowed Jesus; as yet, not as his Apostles; for their call to that Office was afterward (as we shall hear); nor yet, so as no more to depart from him; but there was created in them a further desire of Knowledge of him, and Acquain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tance with him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:330" />38 Then Jesus turned, and saw them fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowing, and saith unto them, What seek ye? They said unto him, Rabbi, (which is to say, being interpreted, Master) where <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or <ns0:hi>abidest.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> dwellest thou <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Christ as he walked, turning him, and seeing two men following him, inquireth of their end, what they sought; to teach us in all our Religious motions and actions, to do the like; for the end will contribute much to specify the Acti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, and to make it good or bad. They give him that ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nourable Title which was then in Fashion, by, and under which they were wont to speak to those upon whom they relied for Instruction, whose Doctrine they desired to know, and with whom they desired to converse, and to learn of him. They asked him, where he abode, or where he lodged?</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 He saith unto them, Come and see <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Our Lord discerning the End of their following him to be sincere and good, invites them to come and see where his Lodging was; for he elsewhere telleth us, that he had not an house wherein to hide his head. They</ns0:note>. They came and saw where he dwelt <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">came and saw his Lodgings (where, or of what nature they were, we are not told) but we never read that he during his whole Pilgrimage amongst us, had any stately or splen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />did Lodgings.</ns0:note>, and abode with him that day, <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The text saith, that these two Disciples abode with him that day; whether onely the two, or three remaining hours of the same day (for it was now about four of the Clock afternoon (which answers the tenth hour ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to the Jewish account) or another whole day, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the Sabbath day, (as some think) we are not told, nor can conclude; certain it is, they abode with him the re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />maining part of that day,</ns0:note> for it was about <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">That was a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bout 2 hours before night.</ns0:note> the tenth hour <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">from four of the Clock till night.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 One of the two which heard John <ns0:hi>speak,</ns0:hi> was Andrew, Simon Peters Brother <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Concerning the call of this <ns0:hi>Andrew</ns0:hi> to the Apostleship, see <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 4.18. and <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 1.16, 17. that was at another time, and in another manner. Christ here only invited them to come, and see where he lodged.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 He first findeth his own Brother Simon <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">It should seem that both the Disciples (after their con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verse with Christ at the place where he lodged) went toge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther to look for <ns0:hi>Peter, Andrew</ns0:hi>'s Brother. <ns0:hi>Andrew</ns0:hi> first found him, and tells him (with great joy) that he and that other Disciple had found the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> prophecied of by <ns0:hi>Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />niel,</ns0:hi> and in the Expectation of whom the Disciples and the Jews lived.</ns0:note>, and saith unto him, We have found the Messiah, which is,<ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">or, the anoin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted.</ns0:note> being interpreted, the Christ <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">The term <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> is the same with <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Greek,</ns0:hi> and both signify the same with <ns0:hi>Anointed</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>English.</ns0:hi> The Article in this place is <ns0:hi>Emphatical,</ns0:hi> not meerly prepositive, as in other places, but signifying, <ns0:hi>That Anointed</ns0:hi>; for other <ns0:hi>Kings,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Priests,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> were also anointed, and God's people are called <ns0:hi>anointed</ns0:hi>; but he was anointed with the <ns0:hi>Oyl of Gladness above his Fellows,</ns0:hi> having the Spirit not given him by measure.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 And he brought him to Jesus. And when Jesus beheld him, he said, Thou art Simon the Son of Jona <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Andrew</ns0:hi> having found his Brother <ns0:hi>Simon,</ns0:hi> conducts him to Jesus. v. 44. telleth us, that <ns0:hi>Andrew,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Simon,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Phi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lip</ns0:hi> were Citizens of <ns0:hi>Bethsaida,</ns0:hi> which was a City of <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi>; how near to the place where <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> Baptized, or Christ lod<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ged, we cannot say; probably <ns0:hi>Simon</ns0:hi> was one of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>'s Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sciples, and came to attend his Ministry, so as the Disciples onely sought him in the Croud, and came with him to Christ. When Christ beheld him, he said, <ns0:hi>Thou art Simon</ns0:hi>; he knew him, and called him by name, and told him his Father's name <ns0:hi>Ionas,</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Math. 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.18.</ns0:note>, thou shalt be called Cephas <ns0:note n="‡" place="bottom">and giveth him a new name, <ns0:hi>Cephas,</ns0:hi> which by interpretation doth not signify an <ns0:hi>Head,</ns0:hi> (as the Popish disputant at <ns0:hi>Bern</ns0:hi> urged to prove him the Head of the Church, as if it had been a <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> word, and came from <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>; or as he pretended, ridiculously enough, from an old <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> word <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>) but a <ns0:hi>Stone</ns0:hi> (as this Text tells us) by which name we find him called, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 1.12. & 3.22. & 9.5. & 15.5. <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 2.9. in other places <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> which signifieth a <ns0:hi>Stone</ns0:hi> also, or a Rock. <ns0:hi>Cephas</ns0:hi> is a <ns0:hi>Syriack</ns0:hi> word, <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> word; Christ gave him the name, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.42.</ns0:note>, which is by Interpretation <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or <ns0:hi>Peter.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> a Stone <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Both <ns0:hi>Cephas</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> are by interpreta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, a <ns0:hi>Stone. Beza</ns0:hi> thinks, that our Saviour did not here give him that name, but foretel that he should be so cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led. <ns0:hi>Causabon</ns0:hi> thinks, that the name was here given to him, and with it a new Spirit; that whereas before he was (according to his Fathers name <ns0:hi>Ionas,</ns0:hi> which signifies a <ns0:hi>Dove</ns0:hi>) fearful and timorous; from this time forward he was as a <ns0:hi>Rock,</ns0:hi> steady, firm, and full of courage and con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stancy; but it is a greater question, how this Text is to be reconciled with <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 4.18, 19, 20. where <ns0:hi>Andrew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> are both said to be espied by Christ, <ns0:hi>walking by the Sea of Galilee</ns0:hi>; and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 5.10. where <ns0:hi>Simon</ns0:hi> is reported to be called, after they had taken a great draught of Fish; and with <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 3.13. and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 6.13. where all the Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stles are named, as called at one and the same time; doubtless, the calls were different.
